slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, shrink, delivery and weak stores, not store hours, to reach 3.0% by FY2028
Gross margin and e-commerce, not wages, cut the margin by 2.35 percentage points in two years
–	Store labor explains only 13%: fewer hours offset about 70% of the wage rise
Management's 8% hour cut targets the smallest driver and could give much of its saving back as shrink
–	Shrink is 3.1% of sales in least-staffed stores, against 2.3%
–	Up to $10M of the $14.5M saving could return as shrink
Promotions are the largest lever: returning to their FY2023 share would add about $9.9M a year
–	Promotions reached 29% of sales; 41% now call Harlow expensive
–	Shoppers come for fresh produce (58%) and convenience (44%)
Repricing delivery and exiting nine loss-making stores would add about $9.5M a year and keep the service
–	E-commerce loses about $10.4M a year; the tested fee cuts $2.8M
–	Exiting nine stores adds about $6.6M; six leases end by 2027
The actions reach about 3.0% by FY2028 for $7.5M of one-time cost; delivery and promotions come first
–	FY2026 income would reach about $25M, above the $20M covenant
–	The 2027 wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, is the main risk

slides.title: The proposed 8% hour cut could give back up to $10M of its $14.5M saving through higher shrink

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Labor    3 Promotions    4 Losses    5 Plan
The proposed 8% hour cut could give back up to $10M of its $14.5M saving through higher shrink
Effect of the 8% labor-hour cut, $ millions a year, team estimate
a year from cutting scheduled store hours by 8% (management estimate)
a year of extra shrink: 0.5 pp rise per 6.0% fewer hours in FY2023–25, scaled to 8%, × $1,503M sales
net saving left, before any loss of shoppers to longer checkout waits or stock-outs
The upper case assumes shrink tracks hours as it did in FY2023–25
▪	All of the FY2023–25 rise in shrink (2.1% to 2.6% of sales) is attributed to the 6.0% fall in hours per $1,000 of sales
▪	Shrink responds in proportion to hours: an 8% cut adds 8/6 of that rise, about 0.67 percentage points of sales
▪	If only waste and receiving errors (65% of shrink) respond to hours, the loss is about $6.5M
▪	Effects on checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted
Even with no shrink effect, the cut lifts FY2028 margin only to about 2.0%, short of the 3.0% target

e-commerce sales, FY2025 (8.5% of sales)

fulfillment: picking plus third-party delivery, net of $2.4M of fees

Two corrections turn the team's 6.1% margin into a loss
▪	Third-party delivery is counted; the team's figure leaves it out because finance books it in e-commerce fulfillment
▪	Only new-to-Harlow sales count; the team's figure treats every online sale as new
▪	Sales that would have been bought in store anyway add no profit, and fulfillment costs are all incremental
▪	Packaging and allocated store costs are inside the finance contribution of 20 cents per dollar
The owners' wish to keep delivery holds; the task is to stop each delivered order losing $10.70 before picking
Sources: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack; team analysis
